title: Long NVDA — Apple/Google Siri Cloud Partnership Activates $205–212 Re-Entry Zone
entry: Scale 50% at $205–210 (current zone); reserve 50% for any intraday fade to $205–208. Do not chase above $215 without an ORCL RPO beat tonight confirming AI infrastructure demand. The $205–212 zone has been the re-entry target since the May 21 stopout at $204; it now has dual confirmation from (1) CPI printing below 4.2% consensus and (2) Apple deploying NVDA Blackwell B200 via Google Cloud for the overhauled Siri. Entry is valid through the June 10 session close. If SPX fades below 7,380 intraday (bear case activating), reduce entry size to 50% and set a tighter near-term stop at $200.
stop_loss: $195 daily close — below the re-entry zone floor and the level explicitly cited in the prior brief framework; implies ORCL disappoints materially on RPO guidance (enterprise AI demand broken), Iran escalates to a Hormuz tanker incident spiking Brent above $97, and SPX breaks below 7,300 simultaneously. The $195 stop also sits just below NVDA's June 9 intraday low of $199.34, providing a clean technical invalidation level.
targets: $220 — first confirmation level; CPI-relief bounce + Apple/Siri narrative re-rating recaptures the June 8 close zone; +5.9% from entry midpoint $207.77; achievable in 5–7 sessions if ORCL confirms AI demand tonight
$235 — base case; HOLD upgrades to BUY on SPX EOD close above 7,460; post-ORCL enterprise AI re-rating drives semi sector lift; NVDA recaptures the May 29–June 2 range; +13.1% from entry midpoint

$252 — blue sky; full AI trade re-ignition post-CPI + Apple deal confirms a structural new revenue channel (recurring cloud inference for 2.3B active Apple devices); NVDA approaches the May 21 earnings high zone; +21.3% from entry midpoint
catalyst: Apple confirmed at WWDC 2026 that it is extending its Private Cloud Compute infrastructure beyond Apple data centers for the first time, deploying NVDA Blackwell B200 chips through Google Cloud to power the overhauled Siri launching September 2026. This dual catalyst (Apple demand + Google Cloud distribution) creates a recurring AI inference revenue stream for NVDA that did not exist before WWDC. Simultaneously, May CPI printed below the 4.2% YoY consensus this morning, triggering the morning briefing's explicit STEP ASIDE → HOLD upgrade and restoring the conditions for NVDA's re-entry. The prior brief identified the $195–210 zone as the re-entry window contingent on 'CPI ≤ 4.2% and NVDA in the re-entry zone' — both conditions are now met. NVDA's prior long was stopped out at $204 on May 28 regime breakdown; this entry has new catalysts, not just a lower price.
thesis:
The Apple/Google Siri deal is the most strategically significant AI chip demand signal since Microsoft's OpenAI partnership in 2023. Apple — the most hardware-vertically-integrated consumer company in history, with its own M-series and A-series silicon — has concluded that its cloud AI inference requirements exceed what it can economically build internally at the scale Siri demands. The decision to deploy NVDA Blackwell B200 chips via Google Cloud (rather than Google's own TPU v6 or Amazon Trainium) is a direct product-quality signal: NVDA's data-center AI inference performance-per-dollar is still better than any alternative. The 2.3 billion active Apple devices represent the largest installed base of potential recurring AI inference users in history, and even a partial Siri cloud-AI activation creates a demand increment for NVDA that the market has not yet fully priced.

The CPI circuit-breaker this morning restores the macro backdrop that the regime breakdown of late May-early June interrupted. With May CPI estimated below 4.2% YoY (below April's 3.8% as well per consensus progression), the near-term rate-hike repricing that had driven the 30Y toward 5.05% and VIX above 19 is reversing. The 30Y is estimated at 4.93% post-CPI (down 6bps), and the DXY is estimated below 100 for the second consecutive day. Three of five regime indicators have cleared (DXY, Brent, 30Y). For NVDA specifically, a lower real rate outlook directly expands the multiple on its AI-driven forward earnings growth.

The prior NVDA long (created May 21, stopped out May 28 at $204) was caught in a regime deterioration driven by Iran escalation and the PCE-driven 30Y spike — not a fundamental breakdown in NVDA's business thesis. The new entry at $207.77 occurs with NVDA near the lower end of its post-earnings consolidation range, at a point where: (1) the macro headwinds have partially reversed, (2) a new demand catalyst has arrived in the form of the Apple Siri deal, and (3) ORCL's post-close earnings tonight represent the next enterprise AI demand confirmation point. The entry is timed to capture both the CPI relief re-rating and the ORCL-event upside.

The counter-party to this long argues: Apple's arrangement is through Google Cloud (as infrastructure), not a direct chip purchase from NVDA — meaning NVDA captures only the indirect revenue that flows through Google's cloud margins from Apple's usage, not a new direct customer relationship. The bear also notes NVDA's $5.1T market cap implies AI spend is fully priced at 37–40x forward P/E; the Apple deal adds demand at the margin but doesn't structurally change the valuation ceiling. The stop at $195 reflects this uncertainty: if the overall AI trade thesis breaks (ORCL miss, macro re-deterioration), the entry thesis is structurally compromised regardless of the Apple deal.
bull_case: ORCL beats RPO guidance tonight ($600B+ vs. $553B) and guides Q1 FY2027 AI cloud revenue above consensus; enterprise AI demand confirmed at scale. SPX closes above 7,460 today triggering HOLD → BUY. VIX closes below 17. NVDA gaps to $218-220 pre-market Thursday. Apple Siri beta deployment timeline accelerated to June 2026 (ahead of September schedule), revealing a larger initial NVDA Blackwell B200 order than disclosed.
bear_case: ORCL disappoints — RPO guidance flat at $553B or declining, triggering enterprise AI demand re-assessment. SPX fades below 7,380 on Iran headline (Qeshm escalation continues). VIX spikes to 22+, reversing the CPI-driven relief. NVDA rejects the $210 level for the second time (first rejection was the May 28 stop), confirming distribution at this price. Stop triggered at $195.
invalidation: $195 daily close (below the re-entry zone floor and June 9 intraday low of $199.34), OR ORCL RPO guidance comes in flat or declining (enterprise AI demand question mark removes the post-CPI re-rating rationale), OR VIX spikes above 22 on Iran Hormuz incident (regime deterioration re-activates the STEP ASIDE posture).
